tasks.title: Email about reading club plans
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Read this email from your English teacher, Mrs. Hill, and the notes you have made.

promptBlocks.subject: Reading club for teenagers
paragraphs: As you know, we are planning a reading club for teenagers at the library. I need your help to decide on a few things.
First, should we meet on Saturday mornings or weekday evenings? Which do you think is better for students?
Also, we need to choose a type of book to start with. Would you prefer adventure stories or science fiction?
Finally, can you suggest one fun activity we could do during the meetings?
Let me know what you think!

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Say which time you prefer and why.
Choose a book type and give a reason.
Suggest one activity for the meetings.
Ask Mrs. Hill about something you need for the club.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Mrs. Hill using all the notes.

tasks.title: Article about reading club
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: You see this notice on a website for teenagers.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: A library reading club for teenagers is starting in your town.
Tell us what you think about this idea.
Would you join a reading club? Why or why not?
What kind of books would you like to read there?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it on our website!

tasks.title: Story about a library discovery
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
"When I opened the old book, a small key fell out and landed on the floor."

taskReviews.scenario: Planning a library reading club for teenagers with an English teacher
taskReviews.purpose: Evaluate and justify priorities for the club (time, book type, activity)
taskReviews.originalitySelfCheck: Unique scenario: library reading club planning. Not a reused skeleton. Notes require justification. No forbidden concepts.

taskReviews.scenario: Writing an article for a teenage website about the new library reading club
taskReviews.purpose: Assess effectiveness and recommend: share opinion on joining and book preferences
taskReviews.originalitySelfCheck: Unique: article about a local reading club. Not a generic 'articles wanted' template. Questions are specific to the scenario. No forbidden concepts.

taskReviews.scenario: Story beginning with finding a key in an old book
taskReviews.purpose: Analyse implications and propose action: continue the story from the given opening
taskReviews.originalitySelfCheck: Unique opening sentence: 'When I opened the old book, a small key fell out and landed on the floor.' Not similar to any previous story opening. No forbidden concepts.
